newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan utilities' Aug electricity supply down yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan utilities' Aug electricity supply down yr/yr.

text.p: Cooler weather in August caused electricity supplied by Japan's nine main power firms to fall that month on a year-on-year basis for the first time in 11 months, an industry body said on Thursday.
Electricity supply in August fell 5.6 percent from a year earlier to 78.43 billion kilowatts (kw), the Federation of Electric Power Companies said.
Air conditioners were used less in August compared to last year when the summer was exceptionally hot, it said.
Electricity generated by nuclear power rose 3.2 percent from a year earlier to 27.7 billion kilowatts (kw).
Utilisation of nuclear power facilities was 94.3 percent in August, up 0.3 point from a year earlier, the federation said.
Thermal power generation fell to 36.16 billion kw, down 12.9 percent from a year earlier. Hydraulic power generation totalled 5.95 billion kw, up 0.9 percent from a year earlier.

The federations' figures show that the nine utility companies in August consumed a total of 2.25 million tonnes of coal, 1.62 million kilolitres (kl) of crude oil, 1.22 million kl of fuel oil, 2.88 million kl of liquefied natural gas and 28,896 kl of naphtha.
